exposure: Peripartum opioid prescription (1 week prior to 3 days postdischarge)
outcome: New persistent opioid use (defined as a pharmacy claim for ≥1 opioid prescription between 4 and 90 days postdischarge and ≥1 prescription between 91 and 365 days postdischarge)
cohort: 158,425 women aged 12-55 years in Optum's de-identified Clinformatics Data Mart Database who underwent vaginal delivery or cesarean delivery from 2008 to 2016, with continuous enrollment from 2 years before birth to 1 year postdischarge and who were opioid naive in pregnancy
finding: Women who receive an opioid prescription during pregnancy are more likely to experience new persistent opioid use.
